name: Alice Springs Desert Park
note: Wildlife and bushfood park 10 km west of town with a nocturnal house, birds of prey shows and bushfood tours; Wikivoyage and Tourism NT both list it.

name: Alice Springs Telegraph Station
note: Historical reserve on the original 1872 Overland Telegraph station with heritage buildings, exhibits and walking trails to the Alice Springs waterhole.

name: Anzac Hill
note: Hill lookout above the town with views over Alice Springs and the MacDonnell Ranges, reached by a walking path from Wills Terrace.

name: Olive Pink Botanic Garden
note: Free desert botanic garden on the Todd River named after its founder Olive Pink, with native plant trails.

name: Alice Springs Reptile Centre
note: Reptile display centre in town with local lizards and snakes and a saltwater crocodile.

name: Alice Springs School of the Air
wiki: Alice Springs School of the Air
note: School for remote outback children that visitors can see on tour from the Royal Flying Doctor complex, next to the aviation museum and cafe.

name: Royal Flying Doctor Service Alice Springs Base
wiki: Royal Flying Doctor Service of Australia
note: Royal Flying Doctor Service base with a visitor tour, museum and cafe, sharing the complex with the School of the Air.

name: Old Timer's Museum
note: Local history museum at the Old Timer's Retirement Village on the airport road, with a collection on early outback pioneers and camel trains.

name: Women's Museum of Australia
note: Museum about women's pioneering history housed in the Old Alice Springs Gaol, with the gaol buildings open to walk through.

name: The Residency
note: 1927 heritage house, the former residence of the Government Representative to Central Australia, now a volunteer-run museum of town administrative history.

name: Araluen Cultural Precinct
note: Arts and cultural precinct with galleries, the Museum of Central Australia and works by Albert Namatjira and other local artists.

name: Museum of Central Australia
note: Natural history museum in the Araluen Cultural Precinct with a fossil dig replica, a giant prehistoric bird and local mammal and reptile displays.
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH (OSM via photon, two sources)

name: Adelaide House
note: First stone building in Alice Springs, a historic house on Todd Mall with early communications displays and tea service.

name: Old Ghan Heritage Railway and Museum
wiki: Old Ghan Heritage Railway and Museum
note: Museum about The Ghan railway with old equipment, photos and several historic carriages to walk through, south of town near the airport.
coordinates_source: wikipedia:Old Ghan Heritage Railway and Museum

name: National Road Transport Museum
note: Museum of trucks and the Road Transport Hall of Fame, with a large collection of historic trucks, buses and motorcycles south of town.

name: Central Australian Aviation Museum
note: Aviation museum with older aircraft showing the history of flying in Central Australia, beside the School of the Air and RFDS base.

name: Strehlow Research Centre
note: Museum and research centre about Aboriginal culture and the Strehlow collection in Alice Springs; named only in Wikipedia's museum category, not checked in a visitor guide.

name: Stuart Town Gaol
note: Historic 19th-century town gaol building in Alice Springs, listed by Tourism NT as a heritage site.

name: Hartley Street School
note: Heritage-listed 1930s school building museum in Alice Springs; in Wikipedia's museum category only.

name: Todd Mall
note: Pedestrian shopping street in the centre of Alice Springs, the setting for the Todd Mall markets and Adelaide House.

name: Alice Springs Markets (Todd Mall and Heavitree Gap)
note: Fortnightly markets on alternate Sundays, the Todd Mall market and the Heavitree Gap market, a recurring weekly-or-less event rather than a permanent place.

name: Heavitree Gap
note: Narrow gap through the MacDonnell Ranges south of town, which the highway, railway and Todd River pass through; described in Wikivoyage's geography section, not as a stop.

name: Honeymoon Gap
note: Gap in the West MacDonnell Ranges on the Bullen Road loop, named as a turnoff on the scenic drive.

name: Pioneer Park Racecourse
note: Racecourse at Pioneer Park where race meetings run; a venue for events, not a permanent visitor attraction.

name: Camels Australia
note: Operator: camel farm north-west of Alice Springs with camel rides, a short enclosure visit and a souvenir and art shop.

name: Pyndan Camel Tracks
note: Operator: camel-riding base in the Ilparpa Valley of the MacDonnell Ranges, offering one-hour and half-day camel treks.

name: Original Glen Helen Homestead
note: Historic homestead at Glen Helen in the West MacDonnell Ranges, the early station and roadhouse site, listed by Tourism NT.

name: Standley Chasm
note: Narrow sandstone chasm with a short walk to the sunlit cliffs, in the West MacDonnell Ranges; known as Angkerle Atwatye.

name: Simpsons Gap
note: Gap in the West MacDonnell Ranges 18 km west of Alice Springs with a walking track, rock-wallaby habitat and a waterhole.

name: Ochre Pits
note: Colourful ochre quarries in the MacDonnell Ranges that Arrernte people have mined for generations, with a short walk to the coloured rock faces.

name: Ellery Creek Big Hole
note: Large permanent waterhole beneath red cliffs in the West MacDonnell Ranges, popular for cold swimming and camping.

name: Serpentine Gorge
note: Narrow gorge with a walk to a pool at its end, in the West MacDonnell Ranges about 100 km west of Alice Springs.

name: Serpentine Chalet Dam
note: Ruins of an early tourism venture (a chalet and dam) beside the Serpentine Gorge area, named as a point of interest by the NT tourism board.

name: Ormiston Gorge
note: Gorge and pound with a permanent waterhole, red walls and a walk to a lookout, a popular swimming stop in the West MacDonnell Ranges.

name: Glen Helen Gorge
note: Gorge and waterhole at the end of the sealed road in the West MacDonnell Ranges, with a resort and lunch spot beside it.

name: Redbank Gorge
note: Remote 4WD-access chasm and swimming hole at the base of Mount Sonder, a refuge for threatened plants and animals.

name: Roma Gorge
note: Gorge with Aboriginal rock art on the 4WD track past Glen Helen, reached with a permit.

name: Jay Creek Waterhole
note: Permanent waterhole in the West MacDonnell Ranges west of Alice Springs, beside the Larapinta Trail.

name: Birthday Waterhole
note: Semi-permanent pool on the Hugh River in the West MacDonnell Ranges, a stop on the tourism board's list.

name: Owen Springs Reserve
note: Quiet 4WD bush camping reserve with ruins and scenic creek country on the Owen Springs track linking Larapinta Drive to the Stuart Highway.

name: Wallaby Gap
note: Sandy creek bed between red rock walls on the Larapinta Trail, also an intermediate campsite.

name: Tjoritja / West MacDonnell National Park
note: National park of gorges, waterholes and ranges stretching about 161 km west of Alice Springs, with the Larapinta Trail and a daily park visitor pass.

name: Larapinta Trail
note: Long-distance walking trail of about 223 km along the spine of the West MacDonnell Ranges from the Alice Springs Telegraph Station to Mount Sonder.

name: Mount Sonder
note: Highest point of the West MacDonnell Ranges and the western end of the Larapinta Trail, reached by a summit walk with views over the ranges.

name: Kalarranga Lookout
note: Sandstone-staircase lookout in Finke Gorge National Park with a panorama over the sculptured hills around Palm Creek.

name: Palm Valley
note: Oasis in Finke Gorge National Park with rare red cabbage palms, Palm Creek pools for swimming and campgrounds; reached by high-clearance 4WD or tour.

name: Finke Gorge National Park
note: Remote national park protecting the Finke River and Palm Valley, reached by 4WD track or tour from Alice Springs.

name: Illamurta Springs Conservation Reserve
note: Remote conservation reserve on the Finke River four-wheel-drive route to Kings Canyon, with springs and a campground.

name: Hermannsburg (Ntaria)
note: Aboriginal community at the end of Larapinta Drive, the former Lutheran mission known for its choir, pottery and Albert Namatjira's home, with a bakery and tours.

name: Wallace Rockhole
note: Aboriginal community and rockhole on a 4WD side track off Larapinta Drive with cultural tours and camping.

name: Ewaninga Conservation Reserve
wiki: Napwerte / Ewaninga Rock Carvings Conservation Reserve
note: Small reserve with Ewaninga Rock Carvings, ancient engravings on a rock outcrop on the way between Alice Springs and Chambers Pillar.
coordinates_source: wikipedia:Napwerte / Ewaninga Rock Carvings Conservation Reserve

name: Rainbow Valley
note: Conservation reserve of striped sandstone cliffs and formations south of Alice Springs, with a short walk through the rock domes.

name: Chambers Pillar
note: 50 m sandstone column rising above the Simpson Desert plain, a walk-to historical reserve reached by unsealed 4WD road.

name: Henbury Meteorites Conservation Reserve
note: Conservation reserve with twelve meteorite craters formed about 4,700 years ago, with short walks around them, south-west of Alice Springs.

name: Curtin Springs
note: Working cattle station and roadhouse on the Lasseter Highway with camping, walks and a stop on the way to Uluru.

name: Gosses Bluff (Tnorala)
note: Meteorite impact crater and sacred ground on the Merrereni loop road, with 4WD tracks, picnic tables and walking tracks.

name: Ross River Homestead
note: Historic homestead and resort at the Ross River in the East MacDonnell Ranges, a base for the eastern gorges.

name: Emily Gap
note: Gap in the East MacDonnell Ranges a sacred gap on the Ross Highway in the East MacDonnell Ranges, a stop on the drive east.

name: Jessie Gap
note: Narrow gap in the East MacDonnell Ranges on the Ross Highway, a quick stop on the drive east from Alice Springs.

name: Corroboree Rock
note: Sacred rock formation with a short walk around it, on the Ross Highway in the East MacDonnell Ranges.

name: John Hayes Rock Hole
note: Rockhole waterhole on the Ross Highway in the East MacDonnell Ranges, a roadside stop.

name: Trephina Gorge Nature Park
note: Nature park in the East MacDonnell Ranges with a gorge, river red gums, walking tracks and camping.

name: Ruby Gap Nature Park
note: Nature park reached by 4WD in the East MacDonnell Ranges, with a gorge and walks along the Ruby Gap creek.

name: N'Dhala Gorge Nature Park
note: Gorge with a rock art site in the East MacDonnell Ranges, reached by 4WD or dirt track from the Ross River road.

name: Arltunga Historical Reserve
note: Ghost gold-mining town about 100 km east of Alice Springs, with an interpretive centre, old buildings and a hotel and camp area.

name: Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park
note: World Heritage national park around Uluru and Kata Tjuta, home to Anangu culture, with walks, sunrise and sunset areas, and a visitor pass.

name: Uluru
note: Sandstone monolith, the Anangu sacred site and Australia's best-known natural icon, with a 9.8 km base walk and cultural walks around it.

name: Uluru Base Walk
note: Walking track of about 9.8 km circling the base of Uluru, taking three to four hours, with the sacred sites marked by signs.

name: Mala Walk
note: Two-kilometre walk from the Mala car park to Kantju Gorge on the Uluru base, a Wikivoyage-listed walk.

name: Kuniya Walk
note: One-kilometre walk to Mutitjulu Waterhole on the southern side of Uluru, with rock art in a rock shelter.

name: Liru Walk
note: Four-kilometre walk between the Cultural Centre and the base of Uluru, about 1.5 hours.

name: Valley of the Winds Walk
note: Walk of about 7.4 km into Kata Tjuta to two lookouts, about three hours, with sweeping views between the domes.

name: Walpa Gorge Walk
note: Shorter, easier walk of 2.6 km into the Kata Tjuta domes, a walk to a gorge with rock walls.

name: Kata Tjuta Dune Viewing Area
note: Short walk up a sand dune beside the road to Kata Tjuta, with views of the domes and of Uluru in the distance.

name: Kata Tjuta
note: Group of 36 domed rock formations west of Uluru, a sacred site with walks through its gorges.

name: Talinguru Nyakunytjaku
note: Main sunrise viewing area for Kata Tjuta, with platforms and a 1.4 km circuit of the Minymaku and Watiku walks.

name: Uluru-Kata Tjuta Cultural Centre
note: Visitor and cultural centre at the start of the Uluru base walk, with Anangu art, galleries, exhibitions and the Ininti cafe.

name: Tjukurpa Tunnel
note: Exhibit tunnel inside the Uluru-Kata Tjuta Cultural Centre telling Anangu Tjukurpa stories; part of the cultural centre rather than a separate stop.

name: Field of Light
note: Bruce Munro's permanent light sculpture of illuminated stems at Yulara, visited before sunrise and after sunset.

name: Imalung Lookout
note: Sand-dune lookout at the centre of the Yulara drive loop with excellent views of Uluru and partial views of Kata Tjuta.

name: Pioneer Lookout
note: Sand-dune lookout south of the Pioneer Outback Hotel at Yulara, with excellent views of Uluru.

name: Naninga Lookout
note: Sand-dune lookout at the north of the Yulara resort with views of the town and distant Uluru.

name: Gallery of Central Australia
note: Indigenous art gallery at Yulara showing works from communities across Central Australia, with work for sale.
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH (OSM via photon, two sources)

name: Yulara
note: Resort village just outside Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park, the base for accommodation, dining, tours and flights to Uluru.

name: Sounds of Silence Dinner
note: Operator: an evening desert buffet dinner under the stars near Uluru, held at a dining area reached by coach from Yulara.

name: Watarrka National Park
note: National park of Kings Canyon and its desert gorges, about 330 km south-west of Alice Springs, with walks and a resort.

name: Kings Canyon
note: Sandstone canyon up to 270 m deep in Watarrka National Park, a headline attraction reached by the Rim Walk and King Creek walk.

name: Kings Canyon Rim Walk
note: Seven-kilometre loop walk around the rim of Kings Canyon, about five hours, with the canyon domes and views of the desert.
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH (OSM via photon, two sources)

name: Garden of Eden (Kings Canyon)
note: Green waterhole at the far end of the Kings Canyon Rim Walk, a short side trip from the loop.
coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH (OSM via photon, two sources)

name: King Creek Walk
note: Short wheelchair-accessible walk at the bottom of Kings Canyon with panels on birds and Aboriginal history.

name: Giles Track
note: Long 22-kilometre track in Watarrka National Park to Kathleen Springs, requiring walker registration.

name: Kathleen Springs Walk
note: Short flat walk at Kathleen Springs at the end of Watarrka National Park, accessible to everyone.

name: Mount Ebenezer Roadhouse
note: Aboriginal-owned roadhouse on the Lasseter Highway about 200 km from Uluru, with an art room for local artists and basic accommodation.
